name: Economic nationalism
summary: Economic nationalism holds that the economy should serve national goals such as power, security and independence, so the state should shape trade, industry and capital flows rather than leave them to markets. Its core tools are protective tariffs, support for strategic industries, restrictions on foreign takeovers and a preference for exporting more than importing. It says little on social or constitutional questions, where its left and right variants diverge.
scope: The mainstream tradition running from Hamilton's Report on Manufactures and Friedrich List's National System of Political Economy to modern economic patriotism and protectionist populism (for example Law and Justice, Fidesz and recent US tariff policy). Mercantilism is covered by its own profile and is only drawn on for its shared logic. Most statements are social or constitutional and lie outside the doctrine, so many answers are low-confidence inferences.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Economic nationalism is about trade and industry, not health policy; right and left variants split, so no stated position.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Not an issue of the doctrine; nationalists differ, some wanting higher wages for native workers and others favouring employers' competitiveness.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The core belief is that markets should serve national goals, so adherents reject the claim that unguided markets beat state judgment on industry.

public-ownership.rationale: Strategic firms are favoured as national champions, but this is usually protection or direction, not nationalisation, and adherents split.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Taxation of the rich is not part of the doctrine; right and left strands diverge.

unions-good.rationale: Some strands protect domestic labor and industrial jobs, others side with employers; nothing in the core settles it.

property-fundamental.rationale: Property is acceptable but yields to national security, as in blocked foreign takeovers, yet the doctrine has no stance on property as such.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Governments in this tradition direct firms toward national aims and block foreign takeovers, which implies more regulation, though it is inferred.

cut-welfare.rationale: Welfare is not discussed in the doctrine beyond cushioning globalization shocks; adherents split.

worker-ownership.rationale: Collective worker ownership is not a concern of economic nationalism and adherents are indifferent.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Security-minded but unrelated to the economic core; no stated position.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Outside the doctrine's scope; adherents split along general left-right lines.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not addressed by an economic doctrine; adherents split.

strong-leader.rationale: Strong states are favoured, but the doctrine is compatible with parliamentary governments such as List's Germany and Hamilton's republic.

state-harmful.rationale: It rests on state intervention to build national wealth and power, so it flatly rejects the idea that the state is harmful.

limit-guns.rationale: Unrelated to economic nationalism; no position.

empower-police-military.rationale: Industrial policy is justified by military power and security, so more defense capacity fits, though police is inferred.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Unrelated to the doctrine; adherents split.

decide-locally.rationale: The nation is the unit of economic policy, so adherents prefer national over local control, as in List's call to abolish internal tariffs.

rehabilitation.rationale: Criminal justice is outside the doctrine; no position.

traditional-family.rationale: Modern right-wing variants are socially conservative while left variants are not; split.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Social issue outside the doctrine; strands split.

abortion-legal.rationale: Social issue outside the doctrine; strands split.

more-religion-public.rationale: No stated position; right-populist variants lean religious, others do not.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Unrelated to the economic core; strands split.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Unrelated to the doctrine; no position.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Modern economic nationalists tie economic protection to national identity and culture, though classical List-style variants say less.

gradual-change.rationale: No stated stance; Hamilton and List sought deliberate state-led change but through existing institutions.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Wikipedia notes that modern economic nationalists often see immigration as diluting national identity and restrict movement of labor, though Hamilton welcomed skilled immigrants.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Subordinating the economy to national goals means resisting supranational bodies that limit tariffs and industrial policy.

free-trade.rationale: List held free trade is true only if all nations adopt it together and otherwise benefits the already-advanced; economic nationalism is defined against liberal free trade.

nation-first.rationale: The core belief is that the economy should serve nationalist goals, ahead of global cooperation.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Foreign policy beyond the economic core; no stated position.

open-borders.rationale: It restricts movement of labor, goods and capital and defends the national economy and identity, so open borders are the opposite.

limit-growth.rationale: Industrialization and national economic power are central aims, so limiting growth conflicts with them; inferred.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Not an issue the doctrine addresses; strands differ, with some backing green industrial policy and others fossil production.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Hamilton stressed applying technology and invention, but there is no doctrine about solving humanity's problems.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Energy independence might favour it, but the doctrine has no stated position.

revolution-justified.rationale: The tradition works through state policy and established governments, so revolution is not part of it; inferred.

experts-over-public.rationale: No stated position; state planners are favoured but populist variants distrust experts.

central-planning.rationale: It directs industry but keeps private firms and markets; wholesale planning is not what List or Hamilton proposed.

socialized-markets.rationale: Ownership form is secondary; what matters is national benefit, so adherents are indifferent.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not discussed in the doctrine; no position.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Not a concern of the doctrine; no position.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: List proposed protective duties on cotton, linen and woollens to let a laggard industrialize, and Hamilton's report urged duties to shield infant industries.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Wikipedia describes state support for industrialization and designated strategic firms, and Hamilton advocated bounties and public improvements.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Not a stated aim; national champions suggest large firms are acceptable.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: It is a nationalist capitalist-compatible doctrine with money and wages intact, so abolition is flatly opposed.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: The doctrine favors state economic capacity, so leaving money to the market is disfavored; Hamilton founded the national bank tradition.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Some nationalist regimes used corporatism, but it is not part of the core.

one-party-rule.rationale: The doctrine is compatible with various regimes, but one-party rule is not needed by it.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Regime type is not addressed; List and Hamilton served different regimes.

democracy-best.rationale: The doctrine is neutral on regime type; contemporary variants sit in democratic populism, but no stated view.

direct-votes.rationale: Not addressed; populist variants may like it, others not.

workers-councils.rationale: Councils replacing parliaments is a socialist idea outside the nationalist state framework; inferred.

right-to-secede.rationale: It centers the unified nation as the economic unit, as List's drive to unite German markets shows.

political-violence-never.rationale: No stated position; the doctrine is silent on violence.

war-builds-character.rationale: Economic power is tied to military strength, but celebrating war is not a stated tenet.

separate-church-state.rationale: Outside the economic core; no position.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The doctrine does not rest on religion, and adherents mostly reject scripture-based law; inferred.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Security and power are core state functions in this doctrine, so privatizing defense contradicts it.

military-superiority.rationale: Mercantilist and nationalist thought treats wealth as a basis of state power and military strength.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Some modern variants stress ethnic identity, civic variants do not; split.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Nationalist economics treats the nation as the unit of interest and rejects class conflict as the driver; inferred.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Land tenure for indigenous peoples is not part of tariff and industrial-policy doctrine, and nationalists who stress a single national economy disagree with each other here.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Nationalists prioritize national interests over foreign claims; inferred.

civilizational-union.rationale: It favors national rather than supranational economic units.

self-interest-moral.rationale: The state's self-interest is central, but personal ethics is not addressed.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The doctrine ranks national economic goals but never says whether citizens' duties outrank their rights; adherents split between liberal and authoritarian strands.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Treatises by List and Hamilton concern manufacturing and trade, and no economic nationalist text takes a view on nature's intrinsic worth.

limit-population.rationale: Mercantilist writers valued a large population as national strength, but modern economic nationalists have no settled population policy.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Industrialization is the central goal of List and Hamilton, so adherents reject calling it a disaster.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Hamilton wanted invention encouraged, but the doctrine does not endorse disruptive acceleration.

human-enhancement.rationale: Bodily enhancement is outside a doctrine of trade and industry, and adherents hold no common view on it.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Whether AI should make government decisions is a recent issue; economic nationalists treat tech as an industrial-policy matter, not a governance one.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Economic nationalists care about strategic technology industries, but not about citizen encryption versus state access.

restore-past-order.rationale: Not a stated aim; List and Hamilton looked forward to industrial progress, though some modern variants are nostalgic.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Policy is pragmatic and judged by national outcomes, though the doctrine is itself an ideology.

direct-action.rationale: It works through state policy and institutions, not direct action; inferred.

means-match-ends.rationale: Adherents judge policy by national outcomes and have no doctrine about whether methods must mirror ends.

return-to-foraging.rationale: The doctrine builds industrial capacity, so it opposes a return to foraging.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Manufacturing and specialized industry are the basis of national productive power for List, so abolishing the division of labor is rejected.

distribute-by-need.rationale: The doctrine keeps market incomes and national, not universal, distribution; inferred.

production-for-use.rationale: Firms producing for markets and national champions are accepted, so the doctrine does not demand production for need.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Profit is accepted as part of national industry; inferred.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: A class dictatorship is a Marxist idea at odds with the nation-centred doctrine.

collective-farming.rationale: Not part of the doctrine; List valued agriculture, but no collectivization.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Adherents see rivalry among states rather than capitalism as the source; Buell linked economic nationalism itself to conflict, but adherents reject the diagnosis.

taxation-theft.rationale: A state-power doctrine accepts taxation, which funds tariffs, bounties and defense.

harm-principle.rationale: The doctrine is silent on the limits of state power over private conduct beyond economic matters, and strands split between liberals and conservatives.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The nation is the central collective unit, so rights belonging only to individuals is disfavored; inferred.

conscription.rationale: Military policy is secondary; no stated view.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Restricting the movement of labor and capital runs against stressing exit; inferred.

state-as-business.rationale: Citizens as customers who can leave clashes with national commitment; inferred.

positive-liberty.rationale: Economic nationalism speaks of national power, not of individual freedom needing material means, so adherents have no common answer.

media-academia-power.rationale: Populist variants say yes, but no stated view.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Not a tenet of economic nationalism.

organic-representation.rationale: Corporatist representation by trade bodies appears in some nationalist regimes but not in List or Hamilton; adherents split.

total-state.rationale: The state directs the economy toward national goals but not every area of life; inferred.

national-rebirth.rationale: Industrial revival rhetoric appears in some variants, but no stated tenet.

territorial-expansion.rationale: List considered colonies and mercantilists sought trade power, but expansion of territory is not a core tenet today.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Outside a modern national-economy doctrine; inferred.

bound-labor.rationale: Bound labor is incompatible with the modern industrial economy these thinkers promoted.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Epistemology is far from tariffs and industrial policy, and the tradition's texts take no side.

universal-morality.rationale: The doctrine rests on national interest, not a claim about universal moral truths, and adherents hold varied views on it.

single-common-good.rationale: The national interest is invoked, but the doctrine does not claim a rationally derived single good.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Not an economic issue; no position.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Nationality law for diasporas is not an economic question, and economic nationalists differ with civic or ethnic emphasis.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language revival is cultural nationalism rather than economic nationalism, and the economic doctrine takes no position.

workplace-democracy.rationale: The doctrine does not seek democratization of firms; inferred.

school-vouchers.rationale: Education finance is not addressed by trade and industrial doctrine, and strands split on school choice.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: State spending and bounties are accepted as tools; Econlib notes mercantilism sees deficits as bad but deficit stimulus is not addressed.

economic-freedom.rationale: The doctrine subordinates markets to the state and denies that freedom needs unregulated markets; inferred.

rule-by-example.rationale: Rulers' moral example is a Confucian idea with no counterpart in economic nationalist texts.

national-self-determination.rationale: Nationalism supports each nation governing itself, and List sought a unified German economy.

force-without-un.rationale: Foreign policy is peripheral; no stated view.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The doctrine is silent on faith versus reason; nationalists include both secular and religious adherents.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Restricting benefits to citizens fits the nation-first logic and protecting natives from foreign competition.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Workfare is not addressed by the doctrine; right strands support it and left strands oppose it.

class-collaboration.rationale: The nation as common interest implies cooperation between employers and workers; inferred.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Preserving national heritage is more consistent with nationalist outlook than sacrificing it; inferred.

dominated-front.rationale: Some strands in developing countries support it, but it is not a core tenet.

workers-nation.rationale: It stresses national over international class organization; inferred.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Gender roles are a social question, and economic nationalism as a doctrine does not address them.

ban-interest.rationale: Mercantilist and nationalist economies rely on credit and banking for investment, as with Hamilton's national bank.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Not part of the doctrine and incompatible with its mainstream; inferred.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Adherents see the state as serving the nation, not a class; inferred.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy independence might favour it, but there is no settled stance.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Modern variants stress national identity; List valued assimilation as national advantage, though not stated for the doctrine broadly.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy view held only on the fringe of some variants.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral systems are not a concern of economic nationalism, and adherents live under both PR and majoritarian systems.

national-mission.rationale: Spreading a government form abroad is an ideological mission, not an economic nationalist aim, which concentrates on the home economy.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: A sociological claim about gender, outside economic nationalism's remit, on which adherents are divided.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Populist variants say so, but it is not a core tenet.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Not part of the doctrine; inferred rejection as a mainstream.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Transitional justice is not addressed by economic nationalist writers, and adherents split along other lines.

night-watchman-state.rationale: It demands an active state directing the economy, the opposite of a minimal state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Not part of the doctrine; inferred.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The doctrine is silent on moral equality.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: A historical-political characterisation that the doctrine never takes up.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Personal law and religion are outside tariff and industry policy, though national unity might incline some adherents either way.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Religious conversion law is unrelated to economic policy, and adherents hold no shared view.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: A religiously driven policy raised in India and not part of economic nationalist doctrine.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Religious instruction in schools is not a trade or industry issue, and adherents split between secular and religious positions.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Marxist state-theory question outside the doctrine.

consent-of-governed.rationale: List and Hamilton wrote about economic policy, not the source of political legitimacy, and adherents include democrats and authoritarians.

trade-surplus.rationale: Econlib describes the pro-export, anti-import attitude as neomercantilism, and Wikipedia says economic nationalists see trade as zero-sum aiming at relative gains.

population-transfer.rationale: Not part of the doctrine; inferred.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The doctrine is state-centred and does not hold to the nonaggression principle.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Nationalists see economic rivalry between states, but do not claim it drives human progress.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Party bans are a constitutional question the economic doctrine does not address.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Republican freedom theory is not part of economic nationalism, although Hamilton worked in a republican framework.

separated-powers.rationale: Not addressed; Hamilton and List worked within constitutional systems.

vanguard-party.rationale: A Leninist revolutionary party is foreign to the doctrine.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Laws favouring the poor are not a stated aim; left strands say yes, right strands emphasise national over class priorities.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: A British housing policy outside the doctrine, with no stated view among adherents.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Labor law is not addressed by the doctrine; some strands protect industrial workers and others side with firms.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Poverty's cause is not discussed in the doctrine, which locates national poverty in weak productive powers rather than numbers.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Modern variants tie economic nationalism to cultural cohesion, but this is not settled across strands.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Sortition is a democratic-theory proposal with no connection to economic nationalism.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Emergency powers are not an economic nationalist subject; adherents split on civil liberties.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Intervention is accepted but this specific policy is not stated.

party-controls-media.rationale: Not part of the doctrine; inferred.

party-commands-army.rationale: Not part of the doctrine; inferred.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Politicians' pay is not addressed by the doctrine, and populist strands lean one way and elite strands another.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Party organisation is not an economic nationalist concern.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Pooling sovereignty in bodies like the EU runs against nationalist control of the economy, as in Law and Justice and Fidesz critiques.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Executive structure of the state is not covered by the doctrine, and adherents live under presidential and parliamentary systems alike.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is unrelated to tariffs and industrial strategy.

clerical-rule.rationale: Not part of the doctrine; inferred.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: It puts national interest first, so working for one's own government's defeat is rejected.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Censorship is not an economic nationalist matter, and adherents split between liberals and cultural conservatives.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Term limits are not addressed by the doctrine.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall elections are not addressed by economic nationalist writing, though populists often favour them.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Foreign policy is not the doctrine's core.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Not part of the doctrine; inferred.

people-in-arms.rationale: The doctrine builds national strength through the state's industrial and military base; inferred.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: List treated manufacturing as the engine of national power rather than agrarian life.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: List pushed to unify German markets, and the doctrine centers the whole nation as an economic unit; inferred for borders.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Populist variants say yes; not core.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Cultural relativism is not an economic claim, and nationalist adherents have mixed views on cultural hierarchy.

death-penalty.rationale: Capital punishment is a criminal-justice question that the economic doctrine does not touch.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: School curricula on sexuality are outside the doctrine; strands split along social lines.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Science teaching is not an economic nationalist issue.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Pornography law is a social question on which the doctrine is silent.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Strands differ between civic and ethnic nationalism.

minority-language-support.rationale: Minority language policy is cultural rather than economic and adherents are divided between assimilationist and pluralist strands.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Exemptions for religious practice are a legal question the economic doctrine does not address.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Mill's view on social conformity is not addressed by economic nationalists.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Creditor and debtor positions both occur, but a nation-first, order-minded doctrine does not call for cancellation; inferred.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Economic nationalists in developing countries hold that real independence needs industrial self-strengthening, as List's argument implies.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Constitution-making procedure is not within the doctrine's concerns.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Some state-led growth regimes did so, but it is not a stated tenet.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: The nation-first principle puts domestic interest ahead of global duties.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Independence in security follows from self-sufficiency logic; Hamilton stressed independence in defense supply.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The method of electing the head of state is not an economic nationalist issue.

central-bank-independence.rationale: The doctrine puts the economy under political direction toward national goals; inferred.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Territorial bargaining in peace talks is a foreign-policy matter beyond the doctrine's economic core.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Property yields to national interest, as in blocked foreign takeovers, which fits the national-good version.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental risk regulation is not a stated position; some strands see it as a barrier to industry, others use it as a trade barrier.

collective-defense.rationale: Military alliance clauses are not part of the economic doctrine, and nationalists divide over alliances.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: International law on annexation is outside the economic doctrine.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Church-state relations are not an economic nationalist concern.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Whether a head of state stands above parties is not addressed by the doctrine.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Unity is valued but force is not a stated tenet.

region-keeps-system.rationale: The doctrine seeks a single national economic system, as List's end of internal tariffs shows; inferred.

sacred-ruler.rationale: A divine ruler is foreign to a doctrine centered on national economics.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Tax structure is not part of the doctrine, though tariffs rather than income taxes funded Hamilton's government; adherents hold no common view.

character-from-environment.rationale: Nature versus nurture is outside economic doctrine.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Not part of the doctrine; inferred.

space-expansion.rationale: Space as a national goal appears in some modern strategic-industry thinking, but it is not a settled position.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Classical constitutional theory is not addressed by economic nationalist texts.

leader-cult.rationale: Leader veneration is not an economic nationalist tenet, though authoritarian variants of nationalism practise it.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family court presumptions are unrelated to the doctrine.

land-redistribution.rationale: Agrarian reform is not part of tariff and industrial doctrine, and adherents split between propertied and reformist strands.

refugee-return.rationale: The right of return for refugees is a conflict question outside the economic doctrine.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Irredentism belongs to ethnic nationalism rather than economic nationalism, so the economic doctrine has no stated position.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Not part of the doctrine; inferred.

women-must-cover.rationale: Not part of the doctrine; inferred.

common-currency.rationale: Shared currencies like the euro cost nations economic sovereignty, a concern behind economic patriotism in France and Poland.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Pan-ethnic unions are a nationalist but not economic claim, and the doctrine takes no stance.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Minority self-government is a constitutional issue not covered by the doctrine.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: The diaspora strategy question is unrelated to economic nationalism.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Historical materialism is a Marxist theory; economic nationalists give weight to both ideas of national power and economic structures and do not state a view.

ban-cartels.rationale: National champions and designated strategic firms are favored, which cuts against breaking up concentrated firms.

no-bailouts.rationale: The state protecting strategic firms and workers from shocks fits bailouts; inferred.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Populist variants say yes; not core.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Gender quotas are a social-policy question on which the doctrine is silent.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Wikipedia says proponents favor protectionism and self-sufficiency, though List-style views stop short of full autarky.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Nationalists accept standards as protectionist tools, but oppose binding supranational agreements.

moral-incentives.rationale: The doctrine is compatible with market incentives; inferred.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Insurrectionary theory is foreign to a state-policy doctrine.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Titles and privileges are not addressed by List or Hamilton's economic writing, and modern adherents are mixed.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: List expected tropical colonies to supply produce to Europeans, but tutelage as moral mission is not stated.

patriotic-education.rationale: Nationalist identity is central to modern variants; inferred.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Admissions and hiring preferences are social policy outside the doctrine, with adherents split.

public-money-creation.rationale: Who creates money is a monetary question the doctrine does not settle, though state-directed finance is compatible with it.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The doctrine is a capitalist-state doctrine and assumes capitalism can adapt through state management.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Cultivating influence in former imperial regions is a foreign-policy position, not an economic nationalist tenet.

delink-world-market.rationale: Poor-country delinking is more dependency theory; List wanted industrializing laggards to protect temporarily then compete.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Marxist concept, rejected by a nation-first doctrine.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Not part of the doctrine; inferred.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Constitutional rights design is not covered by the economic doctrine.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Colonial treaty validity is a legal-historical question outside the doctrine.

elective-rulers.rationale: Hereditary versus elected rulers is a regime question the doctrine does not address.

minority-veto.rationale: The nation acting as a unit is central; inferred.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: A resistance theory from early-modern politics; the economic doctrine takes no position.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Parliamentary sovereignty is not addressed by the doctrine, and adherents live under both models.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal ethics is outside the economic doctrine.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Animal use is not part of the doctrine, and adherents have no common view.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Aristocratic duty toward the poor is not an economic nationalist theme, so adherents have no shared view.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The doctrine is built around active state policy; inferred.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: A Frankfurt School claim that economic nationalism does not take up.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Gramscian hegemony theory is outside the economic doctrine, which does not analyse class power.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Left variants say yes, but it is not a core tenet.

native-born-offices.rationale: Office eligibility is not addressed by the doctrine, though nation-first strands may favour it.

party-own-road.rationale: A debate within communist movements that is irrelevant to economic nationalism.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: It emphasizes self-reliance and self-sufficiency, as List's call to strengthen a nation's own powers implies.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Territorial revanchism is not an economic nationalist claim and adherents are split.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: A question about political leadership of indigenous descendants that the economic doctrine does not address.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: A constitutional value question on which the economic doctrine is silent.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: A historical-moral comparison outside the doctrine, with adherents split along political lines.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: A historical dispute not part of economic nationalism, though Hamilton-style tariffs mattered in sectional US politics.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Monument policy is a culture-war issue that the economic doctrine does not decide.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Public programmes by sex are a social-policy topic outside the doctrine.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: A social-policy dispute with no connection to the economic doctrine.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Civilizational political forms are not part of economic nationalism, though its national-differences logic leans slightly toward cultural variety; no stated view.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The political role of armies is not addressed by the doctrine, although it ties industry to defense.

paid-care-work.rationale: Domestic labor policy is not covered by the economic doctrine, and left and right strands differ.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Economic nationalists have opposed takeovers such as Mittal-Arcelor and Dubai Ports World's US bid on grounds of national security and national champions.

filial-duty.rationale: Economic nationalism is about trade and industry and says nothing on family duty; its variants differ.

office-by-exam.rationale: Economic nationalism is indifferent to office selection, but its nationalist-populist variants favour political appointment over exam elites; inferred.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Variants differ on divorce and the doctrine is silent; modern nationalist parties often defend traditional marriage.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Economic nationalists favour state control over finance and industry, so a delegated recall rule is not part of it; inferred.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Nationalists favour state-directed economies and sometimes state pensions as national solidarity; the doctrine is silent.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Hamilton and List favoured national industry under private property, so common land tenure is rejected; inferred.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Hamilton and List worked within constitutional systems with legislative budgets; inferred.

single-official-language.rationale: The doctrine is silent on language policy and variants split.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Economic nationalism seeks to keep national assets under national ownership, which the Wikipedia article ties to restrictions on foreign control.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: The doctrine is not about racial equality, and its right-wing variants reject outcome-based discrimination claims; inferred.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Economic nationalists are split and the doctrine does not speak to consumption.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Great-power economic nationalists pursue state-first policy, but it is mostly about trade rather than arming rebels; inferred.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Economic nationalism is about national independence rather than domination of allies; inferred.

corporate-influence.rationale: Economic nationalism favours state direction of industry, but its right variants court business and its left variants oppose corporate power, so adherents are split.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine's restrictions on foreign takeovers and its stress on national economic independence; funding of NGOs and media is not covered.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine's preference for national self-reliance over immigration; modern variants such as Fidesz pair it with pro-birth policy, but the core doctrine does not state it.

residents-only-property.rationale: The doctrine limits foreign ownership of national assets but does not address local residents-only rules, so adherents are split.

job-guarantee.rationale: Economic nationalism is about trade and industry, and the left and right variants differ on state employment.

democratic-peace.rationale: The doctrine treats trade and power as a rivalry between states and doubts that economic or political openness brings harmony, as List's critique of universal free trade shows; not stated about democracy.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine's emphasis on state authority to direct the economy; the question is outside its scope.

non-intervention.rationale: The doctrine puts national interest first, which fits sovereignty, but it does not address intervention in other states' internal affairs; split.

industrial-unions.rationale: Economic nationalism does not address union structure, and its variants range from labour-friendly to hostile.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Outside the doctrine; the economic-nationalist mainstream does not rely on minority-conspiracy claims, though populist variants sometimes do, so adherents would mostly disagree.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Outside the doctrine; mainstream adherents of the tradition keep conventional legal institutions such as marriage.

public-access-to-information.rationale: The doctrine does not address access to government information, and variants range from liberal to secretive.

local-production.rationale: List and Hamilton argued for building domestic manufactures and supply for national independence, so national production is favoured; local rather than national scale is an inference.

informal-organisation.rationale: Inferred from the tradition's reliance on states and permanent national institutions to direct the economy.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine's stress on national sovereignty over the economy against supranational trade rules.

religious-nation.rationale: Outside the doctrine; the tradition defines the nation by economic interest, not religion, though some modern variants add religion.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Economic nationalism's core aim is national economic independence, so tribute and submission to a leading power are rejected; inferred from that.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine's focus on the national economy as a whole, which suggests pooling revenue nationally.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Economic nationalism favours state direction of national industry but not common ownership; inferred from the doctrine's focus on strengthening national capital.

defeat-communism.rationale: Left and right variants differ on communism, and the doctrine is about trade, not ideology.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: The doctrine says nothing on how services are delivered, and its variants are split.

religion-illusion.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the doctrine's materialist focus on national power, which has no stake in religion's fate.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: List and Hamilton saw industrial capitalism as a national achievement but opposed free-trade capitalism, so the statement splits adherents.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; variants are split.

socialized-care.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; variants are split.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine, which concerns trade and industry.

treaties-binding.rationale: Not addressed; variants differ on minority and indigenous treaties.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine's aim of building national industrial power, which favours large-scale production over small common-property communities.

majority-settlement.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; its right and left variants differ.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Variants differ: some favour a third way of state-guided capitalism, others sit within either camp.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Not part of the doctrine, which concerns trade and industry; variants differ.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; a typical adherent would not hold this view, inferred from its pursuit of mainstream national power.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Outside the doctrine and left and right variants differ.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The doctrine is about economic policy, not political order; mainstream modern variants work within electoral politics, though some populist forms are authoritarian; inferred.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Outside the doctrine; religion-state questions split variants.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Mercantilism, which shares its logic, treated colonies as sources of wealth for the ruling state, but economic nationalism as a whole does not require empire; inferred.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; variants differ.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; variants differ.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Its left and right variants diverge, and it is defined by national goals rather than a place on that divide.

alienated-labor.rationale: The doctrine treats the economy as serving national ends, not as an arena of class alienation; inferred.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Right variants link it to immigration restriction, but the doctrine itself does not address Islam.

social-market-economy.rationale: It rejects laissez-faire but welfare policy is not part of it, and left and right variants diverge on it.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The doctrine treats economic strength as the basis of state power and security, which presupposes armed forces.

rich-first.rationale: List and Hamilton aimed at national development led by the state, not at leaving some to get rich first; inferred.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Variants differ on alliances; the doctrine stresses independence but does not address blocs.

dynastic-succession.rationale: The ideology is about trade and industry, not succession; its adherents range from republican to monarchist, and it leans against hereditary office; inferred.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: The ideology is silent on the point; adherents' views on credit and banking differ, though some favour national or state banks.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Economic nationalists put national economic independence over outside lenders' demands, as in the policy tradition; inferred.

property-franchise.rationale: The ideology says little on the franchise; List and Hamilton lived in property-franchise eras, but modern adherents accept universal suffrage; inferred.

domination-women-nature.rationale: The ideology does not address it, and treats nature as a resource for national power; inferred.

reification.rationale: The ideology is not Marxist and rarely adopts this critique of capitalism; inferred.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: The ideology is indifferent to press freedom, and its left and right variants diverge on the power of wealth; split.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Hamilton and List wrote within constitutional states governed by law; inferred as a mild positive since the ideology is silent.

racial-franchise.rationale: The mainstream tradition from Hamilton and List ties the nation to economic interests, not race; racial voting limits are no part of it.

online-participation.rationale: The ideology is silent on digital participation; inferred as neutral.

open-government-data.rationale: The ideology is silent on open government; inferred as neutral.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: The ideology is silent on religion and law; inferred as mildly against restrictions.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Economic nationalism is concerned with foreign firms and goods, not a domestic religious minority's shops; boycotts of a minority are no part of it.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Economic nationalism is about trade and industry, not decision procedures, and its left and right variants differ, so there is no stated position.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Economic nationalism says nothing on religious doctrine, and its adherents range from traditionalist to secular, so no stated position.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The doctrine concerns trade and industry; nationalists are split between those who fear oligarchs and those who back national champions, so no stated position.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: A social question outside the doctrine; left and right variants of economic nationalism diverge on it.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Inferred: economic nationalism says nothing on religion, and its mainstream adherents do not seek state atheism.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine wants a strong state serving national goals, which fits keeping police and prisons rather than abolishing them.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; inferred only that a unitary national interest is emphasized, but variants differ.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Inferred from its call for state direction of the economy for national ends, which sits poorly with leaving welfare to charity, though right-wing variants differ.

term-limits.rationale: Constitutional questions lie outside the doctrine and adherents are split.

vote-delegation.rationale: Inferred: a doctrine of state-led national purpose has no place for delegable direct democracy, which it never discusses.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Not addressed; the doctrine focuses on national economic power, not long-run global risks.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Religious institutions are outside the doctrine, and adherents split between traditionalist and secular variants.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Inferred: modern economic nationalist parties and states mostly do not defend husband authority, but the doctrine is silent and traditionalist variants exist.

missingStatements.text: The government should block foreign companies from buying firms in strategic industries.
missingStatements.rationale: Economic nationalists have opposed takeovers such as Mittal-Arcelor and Dubai Ports World's US bid on grounds of national security and national champions.

missingStatements.text: Poor or late-developing countries should temporarily protect their young industries until they can compete with established foreign producers.
missingStatements.rationale: List's central argument is that a laggard nation must first strengthen its own productive powers before facing advanced rivals.

notes: Left-wing and right-wing variants diverge on welfare, unions and immigration, so those answers are neutral. Hamilton's protectionism is described by some historians as milder than its reputation.
